triage.workOrder: C — hand-triage every UNKNOWN and every non-collision over-claim from the production composition root
triage.method: constructor/factory wiring -> concrete instance -> receiver -> target method; nothing demoted on method-name or interface-name grounds

finalCounts.note: Hand-triage recovered 12 boundaries the independent resolver could not follow. The earlier "18 over-claims" figure is superseded: it counted resolver gaps as suspected over-claims.
finalCounts.authorityNote: HAND-DERIVED. These counts include 12 boundaries resolved by reading wiring by hand; the qualified resolver alone proves 82. An automated authority cannot reproduce 94 as of this round.

records.wiring: application.ts:539 `new PostgresSemanticCorpusSourceSnapshotReader(pool)` -> passed as the `source` argument of SemanticGenerationBuilder at application.ts:623 -> `this.source.readSnapshot` at semantic-generation/src/index.ts:292; the route at ai-settings-routes.ts:558 receives the same instance.
records.evidence: readSnapshot has exactly two production implementors (semantic-corpus-postgres:145, semantic-corpus-repository:30) and the app assembly binds the Postgres reader.
records.resolverGap: the constructor parameter is a structural inline type `{ readSnapshot(...); readWatermark(...) }`, which names no class

records.evidence: concrete class is visible in the same function scope as the call site
records.resolverGap: the call sits inside an object literal passed to a factory, so the receiver is a closure variable the single-pass resolver did not bind

records.wiring: application.ts:472 `new PostgresFrontendCommandGateway(pool)` -> application.ts:1217 `frontendCommandGateway: commandGateway` -> the route modules receive it and call `accept` at frontend-command-route.ts:56/108, frontend-product-routes.ts:325/642, sources-routes.ts:186, typed-proposition-conflict-routes.ts:85
records.evidence: FrontendCommandGatewayPort exposes `accept`; its production implementors are PostgresFrontendCommandGateway and InMemoryFrontendCommandGateway (the latter only as the default in server.ts:2244 when no gateway is supplied, which is not the app assembly wiring)
records.resolverGap: port-typed receivers passed through dependency objects

records.wiring: application.ts:521 `new PostgresSourcesProductService(pool, staging, sourcesStage3Pipeline)` -> application.ts:535 `configureSourcesWriteRuntime({ productService: sourcesProductService })` -> sources-routes.ts:351 `runtime.productService.submit(...)`
records.evidence: PostgresSourcesProductService is the ONLY implementation of SourcesProductWriteServicePort; the runtime field is typed as that port and bound to this instance at the composition root
records.resolverGap: receiver is `runtime.productService` where `runtime` comes from a module-level `getSourcesWriteRuntime()` accessor

records.evidence: the receiver is the Postgres comparison repository; `save` is reached on that concrete instance
records.resolverGap: receiver is `input.repository`, an interface-typed member of the module's input object

records.why: the only production-scope call site is behind `testDevelopmentAuth = process.env.VITEST === 'true' && !options.authRepository && !production`. That guard is *false in production by construction*, and mutually exclusive with the Postgres wiring: the guard requires no injected authRepository, while application.ts:924 injects `new PostgresAuthRepository(pool)`. `bootstrapOwner` is not part of the production startup path, and AuthRepositoryPort is also implemented by InMemoryAuthRepository.
records.classification: method/guard collision — the recorded PROVEN rests on a test-only code path

records.why: the recorded call is on FrontendKnowledgeDraftProductCoordinator, not on the canonical repository; no production call site reaches PostgresCanonicalKnowledgeRepository.commitFrontendDraft
the receiver resolves to ProductFindingRepository (a different type), not to PostgresDiscoveryFindingRepository
the only same-named call sites are on a different port that PostgresDiscoveryRuntimeRepository does not implement

records.whyStaticallyUndecidable: the method is `private` with no external caller. Its production reachability depends on whether `lifecycle.start()` is invoked, and that lifecycle can only be started by the application assembly through `options.connectorRuntimeState?.lifecycle?.start()` at server.ts:2968, while the boundary's own `beforeAll`-style test harness starts it separately. Bytecode/static evidence cannot confirm the concrete binding without knowing whether the app assembly enables the durable connector runtime in the deployed configuration; asserting either way would be a guess.

triage.supersedes: The unsuperseded figure of 18 over-claims came from the resolver alone, which under-estimates qualified reachability because it cannot follow object-literal factories, port-typed dependency objects, or accessor-returned runtimes.

machineAuthority.note: What the qualified resolver emits mechanically for all 113 boundaries. This is the figure an adoptable authority would produce today.
machineAuthority.blocker: REVIEW_REQUIRED is rejected by the validator (PRODUCTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED at ts6-phase-b-transaction-authority-validator.ts:826), so a projection containing one cannot pass. The class must be driven to zero before adoption.
